label: fs-every-set-is-open-or-closed
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: The refutation uses the specific counterexample [0,1). The endpoints 0 and 1 are explicitly treated in steps 1.2 and 1.3; the choices of the test points y = –ε·2⁻¹ and y = 1 – t work for every ε>0. The set is a legitimate subset of ℝ, nonempty and not the whole space. No degenerate case (empty set, singleton, unbounded interval) is needed to refute the universal claim, and the proof does not rely on any special property that would fail in a boundary case. The argument that a two‑element set has a minimum uses lem‑finite‑set‑has‑max without issue.
SOURCES: All twelve supplied cited items were inspected: def‑open‑and‑closed‑in‑r, def‑neighbourhood‑r, lem‑finite‑set‑has‑max, def‑max‑min, lem‑of‑abs‑value, cor‑of‑one‑positive, lem‑of‑add‑order, lem‑of‑sign‑rules, def‑ordered‑field, def‑complete‑ordered‑field, def‑interval, and the forward‑ref cex‑half‑open‑interval‑neither‑open‑nor‑closed. Their statements match the uses in the target; no citation is materially inaccurate or over‑extended.
CHECKED: The title (“FALSE: every subset of ℝ is either open or closed”), the public claim, every numbered step (1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1), and all Remarks were read and found mathematically correct and logically sound.
